formulas.rule: Drex keeps every question with recorded confidence >= threshold. The rest take GPT-6.1 Sol's recorded answer to the same question.
formulas.cost_per_1000_usd: mean over cases of [Drex recorded cost_usd + (if any question routed) (GPT recorded input_tokens * $2 + GPT recorded output_tokens * routed/asked * $10) / 1e6] * 1000. GPT list price $2 in / $10 out per 1M tokens.
formulas.latency_p50_ms: median over cases of [Drex recorded latency_ms + (if any question routed) GPT recorded latency_ms * routed/asked]. GPT runs after Drex.
formulas.gpt_only: GPT-6.1 Sol recorded answers on every question. Cost is GPT list price from recorded tokens. No Drex cost.
formulas.drex_only: drex-max-v1.1 recorded answers on every question. Cost is Drex recorded cost_usd.

gpt_only.label: simulated from recorded answers
gpt_only.note: GPT-6.1 Sol recorded answers on every question. Cost is GPT list price from recorded tokens. No Drex cost.

drex_only.note: drex-max-v1.1 recorded answers on every question. Cost is Drex recorded cost_usd.

why: Routing: the simulated per-family map picks the same 7747 question ids E escalated (0 ids differ).

Accuracy: measured minus simulated line verdict is +0.0000. The simulation takes the packed GPT call's answers on routed questions. The fresh escalation call got 0 of 7747 escalated questions wrong; the packed call got 0 of them wrong. Any accuracy gap comes from those calls, since the questions Drex kept are the same recorded answers in both.

Cost: the simulation charges the full packed GPT input once per routed case plus scaled output. The escalation call sent a shorter prompt, so the simulation over-states GPT cost by $11.99 per 1,000 cases.
Latency: the simulation scales packed GPT time by the routed share and ignores prompt reading time, so it under-states the measured median by 12.7 s.
